body.estimand_functional: For a fixed explicit input \(I\), write \(\mathfrak M(I)=\{\mathcal M_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_{\mathcal L}\}\).  For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathcal L}\) with \(K(\theta)>0\), the causal target is \(q(\mathcal M_\theta)=H(\theta)/K(\theta)\).  If a verified rational circuit \(C\) is returned, then \(C(\Phi(\theta))=H(\theta)/K(\theta)\); uniform instance-relative identification need not imply that such a \(C\) exists.  On the obstruction instance, the unique identified value is the nonnegative root \(q=\sqrt{ab/c}\) of \(cq^2=ab\) on \(c>0\).

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite menu \(\mathcal R\) of observational and perfect-interventional regimes is supplied; symbolic identification is uniform over its full feasible image.
sampling_model.units: For inference, regime \(r\) supplies \(n_r\) i.i.d. finite-alphabet draws, independently across regimes.
sampling_model.treatment: Each regime clamps a declared endogenous subset \(Z\) to \(z\) and records the complete joint outcome on \(V\setminus Z\).
sampling_model.overlap: Evaluation separates infeasible menu vectors from feasible vectors having no positive-denominator model.  Inference assumes positive limiting regime fractions and a fixed positive margin for every circuit divisor.  Its variance threshold satisfies \(\kappa_n\to0\) and \(\delta_n/\kappa_n\to0\); the proof establishes the simultaneous matrix rate \(\lVert\widehat\Sigma_Q-\Sigma_Q\rVert=O_P(\delta_n)=o_P(\kappa_n)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No infinite-dimensional nuisance is estimated.  Empirical multinomial cells pass through a verified rational circuit by automatic differentiation; symbolically constant coordinates are exact, and nonsymbolic zero first-order variance coordinates are reported without Wald studentization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithms 1--2 and Theorems 5--6 are sound and complete for marginal and conditional counterfactual identification from arbitrary observational and experimental inputs in recursive acyclic SCMs.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The acyclic-reduction theorem uses this as a base case; the present fixed-decoder output-language impossibility is orthogonal and does not refute it.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 9.10 proves soundness of an extended ID algorithm for cyclic ioSCM interventional effects, and Remark 9.11 makes no completeness claim.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The cyclic semantics inform the model setup but do not address fixed-decoder Layer-3 output-language completeness.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.4 gives finite canonical acyclic SCMs, and the paper reduces counterfactual bounds to polynomial optimization.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Finite response parametrization informs the explicit decoder, but it does not provide rational descent for the source-product image.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algebraic geometry gives exact feasibility tests and algebraic recovery in selected functional causal structures with two binary observed variables.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The algebraic-branch theorem proves non-representability by rational circuits on a different fixed source-decoder conditional-counterfactual instance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The inflation hierarchy converges asymptotically to the compatible set for finite latent causal structures.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The compatibility result motivates exact source-aware feasibility tests but does not give a finite rational identifying circuit for every fiber-constant target.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 characterize source-aligned influence functions and canonical gradients for prespecified smooth data-fusion targets.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The circuit-inference theorem uses this only for regular rational outputs; the algebraic obstruction itself has no inference claim.

body.tldr: Rational-circuit-or-countermodel completeness is impossible even for a fixed finite explicit source decoder: a ternary-treatment instance has supplied cells \(a=xy,b=xz,c=yz\) and a uniformly instance-identified conditional target \(x=\sqrt{ab/c}\), which is not a rational function of those cells and admits no same-instance countermodel.  Thus every total sound procedure with only rational positive outputs and genuine same-instance negative outputs needs a third outcome.  The cyclic machinery still gives exact legality, conditional boundary gluing, terminating verified-output soundness, and regular multinomial inference; constructing a nonvanishing transmitting assignment at every recursive interface remains open.

project_justification.gap: Existing complete counterfactual identifiers return rational expressions or graph-class nonidentification witnesses, but an explicit known source decoder can identify a conditional target through positivity as a nonrational algebraic branch.  Rational positive outputs and genuine same-instance countermodels are therefore not an exhaustive output language for explicit decoder instances.
project_justification.niche: Finite explicit source decoders expose the algebraic distinction between set-theoretic identification on a positive semialgebraic image and membership in the rational function field of supplied regime cells.
project_justification.fill: The ternary-treatment construction proves an algorithm-independent output-language impossibility, while the accompanying SC-CTFID results retain terminating soundness for every verified rational circuit or same-instance countermodel.  Exact cyclic legality and conditional boundary-gluing results identify the separate open problem of constructing nonvanishing transmission through arbitrary recursion interfaces.

body.related_work: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021, Theorems 5--6, proves complete acyclic CTFID over its graph-compatible SCM class; the present fixed-decoder restriction is different and does not contradict that result.  BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies simple-SCM solvability and graph-containment semantics, while ForreMooij2020 gives sound cyclic interventional identification without a Layer-3 completeness claim.  ZhangTianBareinboim2022 motivates finite response parametrization, and NavascuesWolfe2020 with WolfeSpekkensFritz2019 shows that independent latent sources impose nonlinear compatibility constraints.  LeeSpekkens2017 gives adjacent exact algebraic recovery examples.  Here the positive-branch witness settles rational descent negatively for the explicit rational-output language; universal source-preserving boundary transmission remains open.  LiLuedtke2023 informs the multi-regime influence-function calculation, while Tikka2023 identifies cfid as the direct software consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The impossibility result is instance-relative and exploits a known fixed decoder; it is not a graph-class cyclic-identification impossibility, and its permitted feedback edge is inactive.  A complete positive language based on quantifier-free semialgebraic graphs or piecewise algebraic branches is proposed but not proved, and universal nonvanishing boundary transmission remains open.  Explicit response/source tables may be exponentially larger than the graph, with no succinct-input efficiency claim.  The inference theorem is fixed-dimensional and pointwise on positive-margin strata; nonsymbolic zero first-order variance coordinates are reported without a Wald interval.
body.honest_scope: The impossibility theorem is relative to one explicit decoder family \(\mathfrak M(I)\), not to all mechanisms compatible with the permitted graph.  Its declared two-cycle is allowed by graph containment, but the \(Y\to W\) edge is inactive, so feedback is not load-bearing in this witness; the result neither refutes published acyclic CTFID completeness nor transfers upward to the full graph-compatible simple-SCM class.  Established auxiliary claims include exact cycle legality, finite source compression, selected source-realizability calculations, intervention closure, boundary gluing conditional on a supplied transmitting assignment, terminating circuit/certificate soundness, exact evaluation statuses, and regular multinomial circuit inference.  Universal construction of a nonvanishing transmitting assignment remains open.
